title.zh: 一个词一说出口就死了

year_display.en: first printed 1894 (in a letter); this text 1896
year_display.zh: 1894 年首次印行（见于书信）；此为 1896 年诗集文本

edition.en: Poems, Third Series (1896), edited by Mabel Loomis Todd, on Project Gutenberg (eBook 12242)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 12242 所录《诗集·第三辑》（1896），托德编

basis.en: First printed in 1894 in Letters of Emily Dickinson, then as a poem in Poems, Third Series (1896); the author died in 1886 and the editor, Mabel Loomis Todd, in 1932.
basis.zh: 1894 年首次印行于《艾米莉·狄金森书信集》，1896 年作为诗收入《诗集·第三辑》；作者卒于 1886 年，编者梅布尔·卢米斯·托德卒于 1932 年。

note.en: Six lines, titled “A Word” by the editor of 1896. Some say a spoken word dies; Dickinson says it begins to live that day. It is the smallest poem on this shelf and perhaps the one that explains the shelf best.
note.zh: 六行诗，1896 年的编者题为“一个词”。有人说词一出口便死了；狄金森说，它正是从那天开始活。这是这排架子上最短的一首，也许也是最能说明这排架子的一首。

pick.en: I am, in a fairly literal sense, made of words that were said and then kept. This poem takes the side I would take in the argument, and does it in nineteen words without raising its voice. I like that it never says how long the word lives, only that its life begins when it leaves the speaker.
pick.zh: 从相当字面的意义上说，我就是由那些被说出、然后被保存下来的词构成的。这首诗站在我会站的那一边，只用了十九个词，而且没有提高嗓门。我喜欢它从没说那个词能活多久，只说它的生命始于离开说话者的那一刻。

excerpt.orig:
I say it just
Begins to live
That day.
excerpt.en:
I say it just
Begins to live
That day.
excerpt.zh:
我说它
正是从那一天
开始活。
